clue.text: Sort of publication that's repeatedly stern

parts.note: stern in its sense of severe or harsh gives hard
stern in its sense of the rear of a ship gives back

explanation.surface: Some publication keeps taking a severe tone, issue after issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' tells you to use 'stern' twice, in two different senses: first the adjective (HARD), then the noun for the rear of a boat (BACK).
explanation.definitionFit: A book bound in stiff covers is one kind of publication, contrasted with a paperback.

clue.text: He finds it hard to believe that he is taking part

definitions.text: He finds it hard to believe

indicators.note: part signals that only part of the run of words is wanted, the letters spanning them

explanation.surface: A man struggles to believe he is actually participating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking part' reads as joining in, but 'part' alone is the signal: the answer is part of 'thAT HE IS Taking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rejects belief in God finds the claims of religion impossible to accept.

clue.text: Fruit to pack — this will record when

parts.note: dates are the fruit of the date palm
to tamp is to pack down firmly

explanation.surface: Packing some fruit, with a device to note when it was done.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber stamp that prints the day is used to log when a document arrived or was dealt with.

clue.text: A support for vessel coming out of the water

parts.note: a shore is a prop or beam that holds up a ship in dock

explanation.surface: A ship's support stand emerges as the boat comes from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: SHORE here is not the beach but a timber prop that holds a ship upright out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land rather than afloat is the plain sense of being on dry land, away from the sea.

clue.text: Stick to path laid down and don't take drug?

definitions.meaning: the familiar park notice telling people to keep to the paths, an order laid down
grass is slang for cannabis, so the notice can be read as advice to avoid the drug

explanation.surface: A rule tells walkers to keep to the path and also to stay clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is slang for cannabis, which turns a park-keeper's sign into anti-drug advice.
explanation.definitionFit: The park sign ordering walkers off the lawn is a command to keep to the path; read with slang, it warns off cannabis.

clue.text: Decline father's drink

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, and the 's adds an S
to sup is to drink, especially in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone turns down the drink their dad offers.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an offer is to let it go by, refusing it.

clue.text: If you want to stay in Bath, stop it!

definitions.text: If you want to stay in Bath, stop it!

parts.words: If you want to stay in Bath, stop it!
parts.note: Bath looks like the English city, but means a bathtub; to keep the water in, you block the drain hole

explanation.surface: Advice to someone who wants to remain in the city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a spa city in the west of England; its capital letter hides the bathtub, whose drain must be blocked to keep the water from running away.
explanation.definitionFit: The drain hole in a bath must be stopped up with a plug if the water is to stay in.

clue.text: Incentives limit us in a strange way

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of limit us are set out oddly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Incentives curb us in some odd fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that rouse a response or spur action are motivations, which is what incentives are.

clue.text: Cash dispenser appears to make young man tarry

parts.note: to pay is the nautical verb for coating a seam with tar or pitch, so to make tarry is to pay
master is the old title for a boy or young man

explanation.surface: A cash machine seems to make a young chap linger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tarry' looks like the verb 'linger', but it is the adjective, covered in tar; 'make ... tarry' is PAY, a seafaring word for coating with pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer who hands out wages hands out money, so he is a human cash dispenser.

clue.text: Covering material that's used by church

parts.note: the word that, taken as written; the 's (is) belongs to the link

explanation.surface: A roofing material that a church makes use of.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reeds laid on a roof are a traditional roofing material.

clue.text: What brings end of true distinction?

definitions.text: What brings end of true distinction?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so take the last letter of true

parts.note: quality in the sense of excellence or distinction

explanation.surface: A philosophical question about what abolishes real social distinctions.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: E, the end of 'true', is brought to QUALITY, and making everyone the same ends distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: When all are treated the same, differences of rank vanish, so sameness of status ends real distinction.

clue.text: Artist's animal held back by prior arrangement

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another, so it is a container signal
an arrangement of the letters of prior means they are reordered
back says the animal's name is to be read in reverse order

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, a common animal

explanation.surface: An artist's pet was kept back by an earlier arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' looks like part of the surface story but is the container signal, and 'back' turns the animal round. Camille Pissarro was a French Impressionist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Camille Pissarro was a leading Impressionist painter, so the name fits a clue asking for a painter, with the 's matching the possessive.

clue.text: Old lady of Paris taking man to island

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: An elderly Parisian woman takes a man to a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' looks like the French capital, but this is Paris the Trojan prince, whose mother in Greek legend was Hecuba, queen of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hecuba, wife of Priam, was the mother of the Trojan prince Paris.

clue.text: Animal that's vicious in the extreme? Precisely!

indicators.note: the extreme of a word here is its final letter, so take the last of vicious

parts.note: to a T is an idiom meaning precisely or exactly

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an animal is utterly vicious and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits at the question mark, but 'Precisely!' is a piece, not a reply: 'to a T' means exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: The stoat is a small carnivorous mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Game so poor before this replacement

parts.note: taken as written
low means poor or inferior in quality

indicators.note: replacement says the letters of this are replaced in a new order

explanation.surface: A card game is so bad it needs a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' rearranges THIS into HIST. Solo whist is a card game for four players.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo whist is a card game derived from whist, in which players bid to win tricks alone.

clue.text: Mysterious things may be spotted in his study

definitions.text: Mysterious things may be spotted in his study

parts.words: Mysterious things may be spotted in his study
parts.note: read as a scholar whose field is sightings of unexplained flying objects; 'spotted' means seen, and 'his study' is his subject

explanation.surface: A scholar's den is full of mysterious objects.
explanation.definitionFit: A student of unidentified flying objects studies exactly the mysterious things people claim to spot in the sky.

clue.text: The village of Gotham

parts.note: Gotham is a nickname for New York City, so the clue asks for the best-known village in New York

explanation.surface: A clue about a small English hamlet called Gotham.
explanation.walkthrough: Gotham is a real village in Nottinghamshire, but here it is New York City's nickname, and New York's famous 'Village' is in Lower Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwich Village is the Manhattan neighbourhood known simply as the Village, and New York is nicknamed Gotham.

clue.text: One likes pictures from the Orient — awfully nice frames

indicators.note: one piece frames another when it surrounds it, a container signal
awfully says the letters of nice are badly jumbled

parts.note: the Orient is the East

explanation.surface: A film fan from Asia, surrounded by lovely picture frames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns NICE into CINE, which 'frames' EAST: CIN-EAST-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A film enthusiast is someone devoted to the cinema, a lover of moving pictures.

clue.text: Hit difficulty providing illumination

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
a plight is a dangerous or difficult situation

explanation.surface: Running into a problem somehow gives light.
explanation.definitionFit: Light shed by a lamp is a form of illumination.

clue.text: Male doing poorly in post

parts.note: ailing means unwell, doing poorly

explanation.surface: A man is sick in the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail sent out, or the act of sending it, is post.

clue.text: Hard-hearted king called for composer

indicators.note: hearted says a letter is set in the heart of the next word

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A cruel monarch sends for a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard-hearted' reads as cruel, but splits: H set in the heart of LEAR. Franz Lehar wrote the operetta The Merry Widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehar was a Hungarian-born composer, famous for operettas such as The Merry Widow.

clue.text: A line written to sweetheart covering everything

parts.note: a lover is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Someone writes a few words to their beloved telling all.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spread across the whole surface covers it entirely.

clue.text: Situation offered to a big gun, so-called

parts.note: a berth is a job or position, a situation

explanation.surface: A position is offered to an important person, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big gun' suggests a VIP, but it is literal: Big Bertha was the nickname of a huge German howitzer of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Bertha was the nickname given to a giant German siege howitzer in the First World War.

clue.text: Wife's turn to complain peevishly

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
a hinge is what a door turns on, and to hinge is to turn on a pivot

explanation.surface: A husband dreads the moment it is his wife's go to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To moan in a whining, fretful way is to grumble, which is just what peevish complaining is.

clue.text: Environmentalist knowing there's a threat to vegetation

parts.note: a green is a campaigner for the environment
fly is British slang for knowing or sharp-witted

explanation.surface: A shrewd eco-activist warns of danger to plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids that suck plant sap are a garden pest, a menace to crops and plants.

clue.text: Man's surrounded by it

parts.note: read Man as the Isle of Man, which sits in the waters between Britain and Ireland

explanation.surface: A man is hemmed in by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, the island in the sea between Great Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man lies in the stretch of water between Great Britain and Ireland, so that water surrounds it.

clue.text: Steal article that is very minimally protected?

indicators.note: one piece is protected by being wrapped inside another, a container signal

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: minimally means only the smallest part, the first letter, of very is used

explanation.surface: Is it theft to take an item that is only barely guarded?
explanation.walkthrough: 'very minimally' means only the smallest scrap of 'very', its first letter V, which joins the abbreviation for 'that is' inside the article.
explanation.definitionFit: To thieve is to take what belongs to someone else, a plain synonym of steal.

clue.text: Poet's love evident in great composition

indicators.note: in says the letter for love goes inside the rearranged letters
a composition is something put together, so the letters of great are reassembled

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A poet's affection shows clearly in a fine piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges GREAT into TAGRE, and 'in' puts O inside it. Rabindranath Tagore was a Bengali poet and Nobel laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabindranath Tagore was the Bengali poet who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1913; the 's matches the possessive.

clue.text: Female disposing of shells near here? It's hard to say

definitions.text: Female disposing of shells near here? It's hard to say

parts.words: Female disposing of shells near here? It's hard to say
parts.note: recalls the tongue twister about a woman who sells shells by the sea; 'disposing of' means selling, and 'hard to say' points to a tongue twister

explanation.surface: A woman gets rid of shells somewhere nearby, but nobody can say where.
explanation.walkthrough: The tongue twister is 'She sells sea shells on the sea shore'. 'It's hard to say' seems to mean 'who knows?', but it says the phrase is hard to pronounce.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue twister places the shell-selling woman on the beach by the sea, where shells are found.
